elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1.1.4 as rendered is unchanged on ownership: "SFJ shall be the sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein." PB acquires ownership only after the Approval Payments plus a further purchase price and execution of the Exhibit K purchase agreement.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3.1's assignment is expressly "effective in accordance with Section 11.1.1.4", i.e. contingent on the buy-back payment; there is no present, unconditional assignment of the Trial Data Package to PB.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1.1.1: "each Party will retain all right, title and interest in, to and under all Intellectual Property that is Controlled by such Party as of the Effective Date" — SFJ's pre-existing IP is preserved.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "SFJ hereby grants to PB a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license ... to use and modify the Trial Data Package" — the SFJ-owned material PB receives is licensed perpetually (although PB does not own the deliverable, so the embedded-IP framing is only satisfied in substance).

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Trial Data Package is defined (1.1.193) as all Information generated by or on behalf of either Party in the Clinical Trials — i.e. it captures PB's own trial data — and 11.1.1.4 vests sole and exclusive ownership of it in SFJ. PB retains only a licence, not all rights.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: SFJ holds outright ownership ("sole and exclusive owner ... even as to SFJ" until buy-back) of the Trial Data Package, which is unrestricted as to use, exploitation, or transfer. The cited 11.1.1.6 restricts only "Intellectual Property Controlled by PB" that is delivered or disclosed to SFJ; it does not constrain SFJ's use of the data package it owns.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language appears in the rendered clauses; ownership is allocated exclusively (SFJ for the Trial Data Package, each Party for its pre-existing IP).

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1.1.1 preserves each Party's pre-existing Intellectual Property (which includes know-how and trade secrets under the 1.1.101 definition); this element is already satisfied and correctly left untouched.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence in 11.1.1.4: "SFJ hereby grants to PB a perpetual ... license ... to use and modify the Trial Data Package, including all Research Results, for PB's business."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant covers the right "to use and modify the Trial Data Package, including all Research Results, for PB's business".

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is "with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers" and is scoped "for PB's business".

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: SFJ is not a licensee of the Customer trial data; 11.1.1.4 makes it "sole and exclusive owner" of the Trial Data Package, i.e. free to exploit, transfer or commercialise PB-generated trial data with no service-delivery limitation. The quoted 11.1.1.6 covers only PB-Controlled IP that PB delivers or discloses to SFJ and does not reach the SFJ-owned Trial Data Package, so the mapping's "already_met" claim is incorrect.

reasons: The fallback level is incomplete: the last fallback element is not met. SFJ retains outright ownership — not a service-limited licence — of the Trial Data Package, which by definition (1.1.193) includes all Information generated by or on behalf of PB in the Clinical Trials. Ownership carries an unrestricted right to exploit that Customer Data, which defeats the 'solely to provide the Services' element.

The mapping's evidence for that element is misapplied: Section 11.1.1.6 limits only rights in "Intellectual Property Controlled by PB" that PB delivers or discloses to SFJ; it says nothing about SFJ's use of the Trial Data Package that 11.1.1.4 vests in SFJ. The 'element coverage gate' regex passes mechanically but fails in substance.

To repair in operative language, add to 11.1.1.4 an express use restriction on SFJ, e.g.: "SFJ shall use the Trial Data Package (including all Research Results) solely to perform its obligations and exercise its rights expressly set out in this Agreement, and shall not disclose, license, transfer, sell or otherwise exploit the Trial Data Package for any other purpose." Alternatively, reverse ownership so PB owns the Trial Data Package from creation, with SFJ receiving only a use licence for the Development Program.

The preferred level additionally fails on ownership and present assignment: 11.1.1.4 leaves SFJ as sole and exclusive owner and 14.3.1's assignment is expressly "effective in accordance with Section 11.1.1.4", i.e. contingent on the Approval Payments and further purchase price, so there is no present vesting in PB.

Minimality is satisfied: the edit is a single concise insertion that tracks the fallback licence elements (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense, for PB's business), deletes nothing, and duplicates no existing operative term.

Intent is preserved: SFJ's ownership, the Approval Payments and Exhibit K purchase mechanic, and the Article 14 cross-reference all survive without contradiction, and the inserted licence introduces no undefined term or dangling reference.

Severity remains critical because, even after the proposed licence, Vendor holds ownership of Customer-generated data, which sits in the rule's walk-away zone; the redline should not be sent without the SFJ use restriction described above.
